_comment: Findings-check actions (ROADMAP §21b). Disciplined active checks, gated on a discovered service, each ONE scope-gated command whose parser records a plain observation fact (http.headers/tls.info/http.methods/http.cors/dns.email). findings.py then matches the catalog against those facts. These are report-recon, not exploitation — proof-bound, never a scanner blast.

actions.title: Security Header Review
actions.hypothesis: A quick header review surfaces the report's easy wins — missing HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options, a leaked server/tech version. One HEAD request, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records which HTTP response headers are present (a report observation, not a vulnerability)
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — a missing header is a hardening finding, not access

commands.note: HEAD the site; findings.py flags missing/weak headers and any leaked Server/X-Powered-By version.

actions.title: Web Component Fingerprint
actions.hypothesis: GET the page and read its script sources, generator meta, Server/X-Powered-By headers and framework cookies to fingerprint the web components + versions it runs — the input the CVE catalog matches on (§21 detection-coverage). One GET, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records which web components (and versions, when exposed) the site runs — the input for candidate component-CVE findings
actions.does_not_prove: the vulnerability itself — a matched version is a candidate finding, never confirmed exploitation

commands.note: GET the site with headers; the parser fingerprints components + versions from the body, headers and cookies (packs/web_fingerprints_*.json).

actions.title: CMS / Framework Version Probe
actions.hypothesis: Once a CMS or framework is fingerprinted, pin its exact version from the files that publish it (CHANGELOG, Joomla manifest, WordPress readme, composer.lock) — the input that lets its version-gated CVEs fire. Read-only GETs of standard paths, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records the exact CMS/framework version from its published version files — upgrades a name-only fingerprint so that component's version-gated CVEs can fire (candidate)
actions.does_not_prove: the vulnerability itself — a version match is a candidate finding, never confirmed exploitation

commands.note: GET the common version files; the parser reads the version from whichever exists (packs/web_fingerprints_*.json).

actions.title: TLS Configuration Review
actions.hypothesis: The certificate and protocol set are a report staple: expired/self-signed certs and SSLv3/TLS1.0 are common, low-effort findings. nmap's ssl scripts read it without touching the app.
actions.proves: records the TLS certificate/protocol posture (a report observation)

commands.note: Reads the cert (expiry/self-signed) and the enabled protocols/ciphers.

actions.title: HTTP Methods Review
actions.hypothesis: An OPTIONS request reveals whether risky verbs (PUT/DELETE/TRACE/CONNECT) are enabled — a quick, reportable misconfiguration.
actions.proves: records the HTTP methods the server advertises
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — an enabled method is a lead, not proven abuse

commands.note: Reads the Allow header; findings.py flags risky verbs.

actions.title: CORS Policy Review
actions.hypothesis: Reflecting an arbitrary Origin (or allowing null) is a high-value web finding. A single request with a spoofed Origin shows it.
actions.proves: records how the server answers a cross-origin request
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — a reflected origin is a finding, not stolen data

commands.note: If Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflects the spoofed Origin (or is *), findings.py flags it.

actions.title: Web Body Review (mixed content / forms)
actions.hypothesis: A read of the page body surfaces body-level report findings the header checks miss — insecure http:// resource references, a login form that permits autocomplete, and a POST form with no anti-CSRF token. One GET, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records body-level hygiene observations (mixed content, form autocomplete, missing CSRF token)
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — these are hardening findings, heuristic and candidate, not proven abuse

commands.note: GET the page body; findings.py flags mixed content, autocomplete-on login forms, and POST forms with no CSRF token.

actions.title: Exposed Sensitive Files
actions.hypothesis: A quick GET of the usual leaked paths (a .git tree, a .env, a server-status page, an editor backup) turns up source and secrets that shouldn't be web-served. Read-only requests of well-known paths, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records which sensitive paths are served (a source-disclosure observation)
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — exposed source/config is a finding and candidate material, not access

commands.run: curl -sSkL http://{{target}}/.git/HEAD http://{{target}}/.git/config http://{{target}}/.env http://{{target}}/server-status http://{{target}}/.svn/entries
commands.note: GET the common leaked paths; findings.py flags a served VCS tree / env file / status page.

actions.title: Cleartext HTTP (no HTTPS redirect)
actions.hypothesis: A HEAD of plain http:// (without following redirects) shows whether the site serves content in the clear instead of redirecting to https. One request, no exploitation.
actions.proves: records whether plain http serves content or redirects to https
actions.does_not_prove: exploitation — cleartext http is a hardening finding

commands.note: HEAD plain http WITHOUT -L; a 2xx (content in the clear) or a redirect not to https is flagged.

actions.title: Subdomain Takeover (dangling CNAME)
actions.hypothesis: When a host's CNAME points at a third-party service (S3 / GitHub Pages / Heroku / …) that is no longer claimed, an attacker can register it and take over the name. One DNS lookup surfaces the dangling CNAME; the operator confirms the target is unclaimed.
actions.proves: records a CNAME pointing at a known takeover-able third-party host (a candidate)
actions.does_not_prove: the takeover — it lands only if that third-party resource is actually unclaimed

commands.note: Resolve the CNAME chain; findings.py flags a pointer to a known takeover-able service (candidate — verify it's unclaimed).

actions.title: Email DNS Review (SPF/DMARC)
actions.hypothesis: Missing or permissive SPF/DMARC is a routine report finding when the engagement has a domain. Two TXT lookups, no scanning.
actions.proves: records the domain's SPF/DMARC TXT records

commands.note: SPF (on the domain) and DMARC (on _dmarc) in one query; findings.py flags missing/permissive policy.
